text:
incident-bot: ⚠️ Alert: Streaming tail latency > p99 threshold for /v1/stream (hosted-prod). p95 420ms -> 1100ms, p99 1.8s -> 9.2s. Rolling error rate for streaming chunk timeouts: 2.7%. Auto-page to #oncall.

maria_sre: saw this spike ~6:02 UTC. dashboards show spikes coincident with proxy queue depth on gateway-1/2. Client RTOs and stalled SSE connections.

jon_devex: any deploys in the last 15m?

sam_oncall: no user-facing deploys. Last infra deploy was 05:50 for telemetry agent.

leah_support: getting customer reports: 3 enterprise customers saw partial stream freezes; they got 504s when client resumed. They're asking for ETA.

maria_sre: hitting p95/p99 across multiple models, but non-streaming endpoints (sync generate) unaffected. That suggests streaming path (gateway + proxy + websocket/SSE flushing).

jon_devex: logs show repeated socket write blocking in gateway: 
```
WARN gateway/streaming: write to conn blocked for 3.2s, client_backpressure=true, buf=64k
WARN proxy: upstream write timeout after 5s, connection queued=128
```

maria_sre: hypothesis: recent upstream kernel upgrade changed TCP write buffer behavior + nginx/haproxy timeouts expose backlog. Proxy is buffering until chunk size reached -> clients see long pauses.

sam_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) disable proxy buffering (nginx: proxy_buffering off) on a subset (canary 2 nodes). 2) lower proxy queue limit to shed backpressure. 3) enable immediate chunk flush in gateway (streaming_flush=true) for hosted-prod. 4) if that fails, failover affected customers to non-streaming endpoint (sync) with throttling.

jon_devex: applying nginx change to canary nodes now. command: 
```bash
# run on gateway-canary-1
sudo sed -i '/proxy_buffering/s/on/off/' /etc/nginx/conf.d/streaming.conf && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

devops_bot: running playbooks: playbook/nginx/disable-buffering -> started on gateway-canary-1,gateway-canary-2

maria_sre: adding a short-lived routing rule to route 20% streaming traffic -> dedicated-fallback-pool (smaller model variant, immediate-flush). Doing that to reduce load on gateways.

leah_support: shared initial customer message: "We're investigating streaming delays; short-term mitigation underway. We'll update within 30 mins."

sam_oncall: after canary reload: p95 dropped from 1.1s to 380ms on canary traffic. p99 decreased too. Looks promising.

maria_sre: proceeding to roll change to all gateways with 2 node rolling restart. Also lowering haproxy queue length and timeouts: 
```
# haproxy cfg snippet
timeout client 30s -> 15s
maxconn 2000 -> 1500
nbthread 4 -> 8
```

jon_devex: note: increasing threads to reduce syscall latency but keep connection limits tighter to prevent large queues.

incident-bot: Pager silence requested by sam_oncall for 15 minutes.

sam_oncall: rolled nginx change across all gateways. Restarted one at a time. Observed brief reconnects for ~1% of streaming clients. p95 globally now ~300-420ms, p99 ~920ms. Error rate down to 0.6%.

maria_sre: pushed gateway change to enable streaming_flush in config and redeployed. Verified in logs: 
```
INFO gateway/streaming: flush policy=immediate, chunk_size=8k
INFO gateway/streaming: client write latency median 2ms
```

leah_support: customers A and B confirmed improved behavior; one customer still sees occasional pauses (client app uses aggressive batch acking). Support suggested client-side backoff adjustments.

product_pm: quick ask — any risk of data loss with immediate_flush or disabling proxy_buffering?

jon_devex: disabling proxy_buffering and immediate_flush only affects delivery semantics (smaller chunks, more TCP writes). No message loss expected; we preserve ordering. Memory use on gateways up ~6% due to more in-flight buffers.

maria_sre: monitoring memory. If it grows beyond 15% we will throttle streaming concurrency.

sam_oncall: follow-ups: 1) create postmortem draft, 2) put a short-term runtime config guard to disable proxy_buffering per-customer, 3) add metric alert for proxy queue depth crossing 75%.

leah_support: reporting impact: ~4200 affected streaming sessions in the 20-minute window, 13 sessions escalated to paid enterprise support. No data corruption reports.

jon_devex: logs from gateway showing root cause pattern: when client TCP window shrinks due to client GC/backpressure, gateway used larger kernel write bursts which hit proxy buffer limits, causing proxy to hold chunks until threshold -> long pauses. Small chunk immediate flush reduces pause.

maria_sre: long-term actions: 1) add backpressure-aware flush policy, 2) improve client SDKs to expose streaming backpressure hints, 3) tune proxy defaults, 4) add synthetic streaming tail tests (p99 under slow-client).

incident-bot: Incident severity lowered to SEV3 — degraded but mitigation confirmed. Owner: maria_sre.

sam_oncall: handing off to maria for postincident tasks — I'll be available for follow-ups.

maria_sre: starting postmortem doc now. Will include timeline, mitigations, customer list, runbook changes, and a proposed rollback plan if memory grows.

leah_support: will send customers an update with ETA for postmortem (EOD).

devops_bot: ticket created: INF-4213 "Streaming stalls: proxy buffering interaction with client backpressure" assigned to infra-team.

jon_devex: thanks team. keep watch for any regressions.

sam_oncall: closing page. staying pingable. :white_check_mark:
